questions.question: What scope should this /ship BK-389 delivery take?
BK-399: what should the kernel's listings do with a stored key that the key rule would refuse or that isn't canonical (e.g. `a\b` written by another tool, or a stored `\`)?

options.label: Omit it (Recommended)
options.description: Listings, glob and the folder aggregate skip the entry, and the kernel logs it once per listing. It is never presented under a key that names another node (today `a\b` folds to `a/b`). A recursive delete_folder over such a folder answers DirectoryNotEmpty, which is truthful. It stays reachable only through native addressing and unwrap().

options.label: Yield it folded
options.description: Keep today's Memory shape: RemotePath folds `a\b` to `a/b`. That collides with a real `a/b`, which is the collision BE-029 withdrew. A stored `\` still makes the whole listing raise.

options.label: Raise InvalidPath
options.description: The listing fails on the first such entry. That is loud and honest, but one foreign key makes the whole folder unlistable, and delete_folder too.

questions.question: The kernel encodes BE-017's folder modified_at rule (the latest known time, the datetime.min sentinel skipped, None when nothing is known), but that spec amendment is assigned to BK-394. Where should the clause land?

options.label: Move it here (Recommended)
options.description: Add the BE-017 aggregation paragraph in this PR, so the kernel's cell traces to a clause before it is written (SPEC→TEST, Rule 1). The note that Graph answers its folder item's own time until step 7 stays with BK-394. The BK-394 dossier gets a one-line pointer.

options.label: Leave it with BK-394
options.description: Tag the kernel cell BE-017 now, with the rule unstated until BK-394. That is a test asserting more than its spec says, for one PR's lifetime.

questions.question: How should the fake-driver suite cover both runtimes (the hand-written async kernel and the unasync-generated sync one)?

options.label: One cell table, two runners (Recommended)
options.description: Cells are data: driver arrangement, faults, operation and arguments, expected answer and post-state. A sync runner and an async runner execute every cell, so the generated twin is held to the same answers. The sync-only layer (read_seekable, open_atomic, BinaryIO read) gets its own cells.

options.label: Async tests + parity check
options.description: Full suite on the async kernel only. The sync twin is trusted through the generation drift check plus a short smoke set. Cheaper, but a hand-written sync-layer defect, or a replacement-map slip, reaches only the smoke set.
